Subject: Mid-contract expansion inquiry — next steps

Hi Kimberly,

Quick one — BrightWave is seeing sustained higher inference volume after our new feature rollout (attached q3_usage_summary.csv). We expect another ~2.2–2.6x growth over the next 6 months and want to expand capacity mid-contract. Our renewal anniversary is 2027-01-12, so co-terming is important for our finance team.

Could you send options for:
- staged top-up vs immediate annualize (impact on invoicing)
- blended discounting for a multi-tranche expansion (we prefer predictable unit cost)
- how credits / unused reserved units carry forward if we split invoices

Also, procurement will need a targeted PO timeline and an initial quote to circulate. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that’s easier.

Thanks,
Ava Reynolds
Procurement Lead, BrightWave
A: procurement@brightwave.ai

Attachments: q3_usage_summary.csv (csv)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Reynolds <procurement@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-12T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract expansion inquiry — next steps

Hi Ava — thanks for the usage file, looks clean. I looped in Ben (AE) and Jordan (finance ops) to help scope a few workable commercial paths.

High level: we can support both staged top-ups and an immediate annualized add-on. Below are three concrete options (ballpark numbers; see attached proposal PDF for line-item math):

Option A — Immediate annualize (simple co-term)
- Add new committed units now, annualize pricing to your Jan renewal date
- Flat blended discount of 18% on incremental committed units
- Single invoice + one amendment (clean procurement path)
- Pro: simplest accounting; Con: larger immediate spend

Option B — Staged ladder (recommended for predictability)
- 3 tranches over 6 months (0, +40%, +80% of projected peak)
- Laddered blended discounts: 8% first tranche / 14% second / 20% final
- Invoices issued per tranche; at renewal we true-up and convert to co-term annual commitment with weighted blended rate
- Pro: spreads cashflow and aligns capacity to realized usage; Con: slightly more contract complexity

Option C — Burst buffer + on-demand top-up (minimal commitment)
- Keep current commit; provide a charged burst bucket with lower-tier discount (4%)
- Best for short-lived spikes, not for multi-quarter growth

Operational notes:
- We can do invoice splitting (separate POs) and track credits per invoice for a true-up at co-term.
- Credits are tracked at the committed-unit level and will be applied before any on-demand charges.
- Legal can issue a single amendment that enumerates the tranche schedule to avoid multiple SOWs.

Next steps: if Option B looks good, Ben and I can draft the amendment + schedule and share a redline-ready PDF. Can you confirm the preferred procurement timeline (target PO date)? I’ve attached a short proposal (BrightWave_Renewal_Proposal_v3.pdf) with detailed unit economics.

—
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: BrightWave_Renewal_Proposal_v3.pdf (pdf)

Kim / Jordan —
Forwarding Ava’s ask and Kim’s initial commercial options. I ran the numbers with finance and recommend we hold the final blended discount ceiling at 20% for the last tranche, but we can flex the middle tranche up to 16% to close. A few internal asks before we send a redline-ready amendment:

1) Jordan — confirm whether we can accept separate POs for tranche invoices and still issue a single combined amendment at co-term. Also confirm how credits will show on the renewal invoice (line-item vs aggregate).
2) Kim — will legal be okay with a tranche schedule attachment (dates + committed units) in lieu of multiple SOWs? That keeps signature overhead low.

I’ve penciled in a 30-min call with BrightWave on Tue 2026-09-22 at 10:00 PT (tentative) — can you both confirm?

Thanks,
Ben
Account Director, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
